cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: There are three main types of habitat: wetland, grassland and woodland.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: The woods are well established and varied, with an oak plantation, and other areas of

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: mixed species.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: The wetland is quite varied, too.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: The original farmland was dug up around 40 years ago to extract gravel.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: Once this work was completed, the gravel pits filled with water, forming the two large

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: lakes.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: There are also several smaller ones, ponds and a stream that flows through the park.

cues.speaker: HN
cues.text: OK, so I suppose with these different habitats there's quite a variety of wildlife.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: There certainly is – a lot of different species of birds and insects, and also animals

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: like deer and rabbits.

cues.speaker: HN
cues.text: And I understand you organise educational visits for school parties.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: That's right. We can organise a wide range of activities and adapt them to suit all ages.

cues.speaker: HN
cues.text: Can you give me some examples of the activities?

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: Well, one focus is on science, where we help children to discover and study plants, trees

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: and insects. They also collect and analyse data about the things they see.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: Another focus is on geography.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: The park is a great environment to learn and practice reading a map and using a compass

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: to navigate around the park.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: Yes, we do.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: For instance, the children can explore how the use of the land has changed over time.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: Then there's leisure and tourism.

cues.speaker: HN
cues.text: That focuses on your visitors, I would imagine.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: Yes, mostly.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: The children find out about them, their requirements, the problems they may cause and how

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: we manage these.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: And another subject we cover is music: here the children experiment with natural

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: materials to create sounds and explore rhythm and tempo.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: And of course, all the activities are educational, too.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: Learning outside the classroom encourages children to be creative, and to explore and

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: discover for themselves.

cues.speaker: HN
cues.text: I would imagine they get a sense of freedom that might not be a normal part of their

cues.speaker: HN
cues.text: lives.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: That's right.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: And very often the children discover that they can do things they didn't know they could

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: do, and they develop new skills. This gives them greater self-confidence.

cues.speaker: HN
cues.text: It sounds great. So, what about the practical side of it?

cues.speaker: HN
cues.text: How much does it cost for a full-day visit?

cues.speaker: HN
cues.text: We would expect to bring between 30 and 40 children.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: If there are over 30, it costs £4.95 for each child who attends on the day.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: We invoice you afterwards, so you don't pay for children who can't come because of

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: sickness, for example.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: There's no charge for leaders and other adults – as many as you want to bring.

cues.speaker: HN
cues.text: That sounds very fair. Well, thanks for all the information.

cues.speaker: HN
cues.text: I need to discuss it with my colleagues, and I hope to get back to you soon to make a

cues.speaker: HN
cues.text: booking.

cues.speaker: LY
cues.text: We'll look forward to hearing from you. Goodbye.
